findings.title: Every app's import() runs eagerly when the module loads, so nothing is lazy-loaded
findings.body:
Each value in the `appStore` object is a call like `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`. These calls run as soon as the object literal is evaluated, which happens the first time anything imports `@calcom/app-store`.

As a result, all 28 app packages are still loaded on startup, even in requests that never touch them. The PR's goal of async/lazy loading is not achieved; the only effect is that every consumer now has to `await`.

There is also a reliability cost. If any one app module throws while it is being evaluated, its promise rejects with nobody awaiting it. Node then reports an `unhandledRejection` (which crashes the process by default on Node 15+), even if that app is never used.

To get real lazy loading, store thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and call them at the lookup sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves errors unhandled
findings.body:
The callback was changed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`.

`forEach` throws away the promises the callback returns, which has three consequences:
- The `try/catch` around it (lines 124-139) can no longer catch anything. Before this change it at least caught synchronous `getCalendar` / CalendarService constructor errors.
- A rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection, which can crash the Node process.
- The function returns `true` and sends emails without waiting for the calendar or video deletions.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block instead.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves errors unhandled
findings.body:
This has the same problem as vital/lib/reschedule.ts. `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })` discards the promises it creates.

The enclosing `try/catch` (lines 124-139) therefore never catches anything. Errors from `getCalendar` or from the calendar/video deletion become unhandled rejections, which can crash the process. The deletions are also never awaited before the function returns.

Replace this with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires async forEach without awaiting; getCalendar failures become unhandled rejections
findings.body:
`requestReschedule` now uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })`. Because the promises are discarded, the mutation goes on to send emails and webhooks and then resolves without knowing whether any calendar or video event was deleted.

Any rejection from `getCalendar` (for example a CalendarService constructor failing to parse or decrypt the key) or from `deleteEvent` / `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. It does not become a tRPC error.

Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`, optionally with per-item `.catch` and logging.

findings.title: getCalendar promise is created and dropped for non-"calendar" variants, risking unhandled rejection
findings.body:
In `getCalendarCredentials`, `getCalendar(credential)` is called for every credential of every `_calendar` app. That includes `*_other_calendar` CRM apps whose `variant` is not `"calendar"`, and for those the result is thrown away (`return app.variant === "calendar" ? [...] : []`).

`getCalendar` is now async, so a failure while constructing the service becomes a rejected promise that nobody awaits. Examples are `symmetricDecrypt` failing in the CloseCom/Salesforce services, or a schema parse error. That surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of an error the caller can handle.

It also needlessly loads and instantiates services for credentials that are never used. Only call `getCalendar` when `app.variant === "calendar"`.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel branch still uses forEach(async) so calendar deletions are never awaited
findings.body:
The non-credentialId branch was correctly converted to a `for...of` loop with `await getCalendar`. The recurring branch was only patched to `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential)` inside `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)`.

In that branch, `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` runs only after the awaits. By then `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has usually already run, and `sendCancelledEmails` and the response go out first. Deletion failures there are unhandled rejections.

The extra `await getCalendar` adds one more async hop before anything is recorded. Convert this to a `for...of` loop that pushes the `deleteEvent` promises, as was done for the sibling branch.
